attribution_limitations: The abstract gives the age as 33 years and the case presentation gives 32 years.
The discussion says the 70/42 mm Hg blood pressure did not coincide with the moment of acute bradycardia (heart rate 20), although Table 2 lists it under "During arrhythmia".
One sentence says the patient remained hemodynamically stable for the remainder of the procedure, but sudden bradycardia and hypotension are reported later during the same procedure.
The authors call the event a peri-arrest situation, pericardiac arrest, peri-cardiac arrest and bradyarrhythmia leading to pericardiac arrest.
High spinal and a vasovagal response to tourniquet pain are discussed as possible explanations and judged less likely or unlikely.
The title and conclusion present the event as a serious adverse effect of low-dose dexmedetomidine, while the discussion also weighs other explanations.
The abstract says intravenous atropine and ephedrine without saying whether intravenous applies to ephedrine.
The block level is reported once after injection and once as assessed promptly after the patient stabilized, without saying whether these are the same assessment.
The pre-operative baseline heart rate called normal in the discussion is not stated to be the Table 2 baseline heart rate of 78.
A similar procedure on the medial malleolus is described only as using wire fixation; which steps were similar is not stated.
The authors suggest the patient's physically active status may have predisposed him to bradycardia through high vagal tone.
